title: Angels and Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Angels worship Christ, serve around His mission, and will accompany His return in glory. Their relationship to Him displays His supremacy over every created power.
summary: Angels worship Christ, serve around His mission, and will accompany His return in glory. Their relationship to Him displays His supremacy over every created power.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is superior to angels as the eternal Son of God, the incarnate Savior, the risen Lord, and the coming King.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Angels appear throughout the earthly ministry of Jesus. They announce His birth, minister after His temptation, testify at His resurrection, and point His followers to the truth of what God has done.

Angels do not compete with Christ. Their ministry exists around His glory and mission. They worship Him because He is greater than they are.

Hebrews makes Christ’s superiority to angels unmistakable. The Son is not a servant among servants. He is the radiance of God’s glory, the exact representation of His being, and the One whom angels worship.

Christ will also come in glory with His angels. Their presence at His return magnifies His kingship, judgment, and triumph.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
This doctrine protects the church from lowering Christ beneath His biblical glory. Any teaching that makes Jesus merely angelic, created, or one spiritual power among many is false.

It also shows how rightly understood angels lead believers to worship Christ more, not less. Angelic ministry is Christ-centered when it is received according to Scripture.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Keep Christ above every spiritual being in your worship, doctrine, and confidence. Do not allow interest in angels to distract from the Savior. Read every angelic appearance in Scripture as part of God’s larger purpose to exalt Christ and accomplish redemption.
